name: critical-path isolation by controlled removal
question: Which path limits the design to 65-73 MHz? Iteration 6 attributed it to the 32-bit accumulator feedback loop. That attribution was an assumption, not a measurement. This iteration measures it.

method.technique: controlled removal: each candidate path is deleted from an otherwise identical design, and the resulting Fmax is compared against the baseline
method.pnr: nextpnr-xilinx (openXC7), chipdb xc7a200tfbg484-2, xdc clock constrained to 15.385 ns (65 MHz), placer sa, router router1, seed 3
method.note: all three runs use identical settings, so the Fmax difference is attributable to the removed path alone

runs.removed: the accumulator feedback: out_next no longer adds to attn_out, so the 32-bit register-to-register loop is broken
the score multiply: score_acc accumulates q_ext instead of q_ext * kq_ext

findings.claim: Removing the 32-bit accumulator feedback did NOT raise Fmax: it fell from 71.86 MHz to 59.77 MHz. The accumulator loop is therefore not the limiter, and iteration 6's attribution was wrong.
findings.correction: Iteration 6 stated 'the critical path is the 32-bit accumulator feedback loop'. That was an assumption. The measurement says otherwise. The correction is kept in the record rather than erased.

findings.claim: Removing the (ACT_BITS x QUANT_W) score multiply changed Fmax from 71.86 MHz to 74.13 MHz, a 3.2% change. The score arithmetic is not the limiter either.

Both candidate removals leave Fmax in the 60-74 MHz band, so the limiter is a path neither variant touched: the KV-cache read mux. Each channel reads one QUANT_W-bit field out of a SLOTS-entry array with a dynamic index (slot_ptr), so every channel carries a 32-to-1 mux, and the eight channel muxes, the sign select, the add and the accumulator mux all sit in series behind it.
findings.status: MEASURED (by exclusion: two independent candidate removals leave the limit in place)
findings.action: Pipeline the KV read: fetch slot N+1 while accumulating slot N, so the mux and the add are in different cycles. This costs one extra cycle per token (18 -> 19) and needs a lookahead of one slot, with the last slot handled specially.

decision: REJECT the accumulator-pipelining plan proposed in iteration 6; ADOPT KV-read pipelining as the next design change
decision_rationale: The measurement contradicts the plan. Pipelining the accumulator would not have bought frequency.
The measured limiter is the KV-cache read mux, so that is where a pipeline stage has to go.
The KV-read pipeline also removes the mux from the accumulator's input path, which may improve the accumulator's own timing as a side effect; that is a hypothesis for the next iteration, not a claim.

cost_preview.expected_benefit: the 32-to-1 mux leaves the critical path; the achievable Fmax is NOT yet known and must be measured

still_open: The KV-read pipeline has not been built or measured yet: iteration 8.
The openXC7 packer defect still blocks the bitstream; the packer failure appeared in all three runs above regardless of the removed path, so the toolchain issue is independent of the critical path.
No silicon measurement: the Digilent HS2 was disconnected throughout.
method_note: This iteration changed no claim without a measurement. It also changed a previous claim - iteration 6's critical-path attribution - on the strength of the exclusion experiment. Both are in the record.
